subject: ARA
label: Grade 02
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 02 Arabic, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 4 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Short words and sentences
modules.outcome: read and write short words and sentences
modules.intro: In this unit, 'Short words and sentences', you learn to read and write short words and sentences. Lessons are short and playful, with objects, pictures and talk. You see it, say it, then do it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Short words and sentences' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: read and write short words and sentences, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: هذا كتاب. هذه قطة. أنا أحب مدرستي. (This is a book. This is a cat. I love my school.) Method: Model run for 'Short words and sentences'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Read and write short words and sentences: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Read three short words and write them from right to left. وَلَدٌ [a boy], بِنْتٌ [a girl], كِتَابٌ [a book]. Say the letters one by one, then blend them. Copy each word twice, joining the letters that join and lifting the pencil after ا and د.

Step 2, Build a sentence with هَذَا or هَذِهِ. هَذَا وَلَدٌ. [This is a boy.] هَذِهِ بِنْتٌ. [This is a girl.] هَذَا كِتَابٌ. [This is a book.] Use هَذَا for a masculine word and هَذِهِ for a feminine word.

Step 3, Add the word الْ [the] and a place. الْوَلَدُ فِي الْبَيْتِ. [The boy is in the house.] الْكِتَابُ عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ. [The book is on the table.] Read each sentence aloud and point to every word as you go.

Step 4, Say a sun-letter word. With الشَّمْسُ [the sun] the l of ال is not pronounced; we say ash-shams and the next letter has a shadda (ّ). Read: الشَّمْسُ سَاطِعَةٌ. [The sun is bright.] Compare الْقَمَرُ [the moon], where l is said.

Step 5, Fix an error. A child writes the words of a sentence joined together or reads الشَّمْسُ as al-shams. Correction: leave a space between words and read ash-shams. Also copy كِتَابٌ carefully: ك then ت then ا then ب, without losing the dots.

Step 6, Your turn: write a sentence saying the girl is in the house, and one for the sun. Model answer: الْبِنْتُ فِي الْبَيْتِ. [The girl is in the house.] الشَّمْسُ سَاطِعَةٌ. [The sun is bright.] Read both aloud.

modules.title: At school
modules.outcome: name school objects and give classroom commands
modules.intro: In this unit, 'At school', you learn to name school objects and give classroom commands. Lessons are short and playful, with objects, pictures and talk. You see it, say it, then do it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'At school' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: name school objects and give classroom commands, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: abi (my father), ummi (my mother), hadha baytee (this is my house). hadha kitab (this is a book), hadha qalam (this is a pen). Method: Model run for 'At school'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Name school objects and give classroom commands: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Name school objects. كِتَابٌ [book], قَلَمٌ [pen], دَفْتَرٌ [notebook], مِسْطَرَةٌ [ruler], حَقِيبَةٌ [bag], كُرْسِيٌّ [chair], طَاوِلَةٌ [table], سَبُّورَةٌ [board]. Touch each object and say: هَذَا قَلَمٌ، هَذِهِ مِسْطَرَةٌ. [This is a pen, this is a ruler.]

Step 2, Learn classroom commands to one boy. اجْلِسْ [Sit], قِفْ [Stand], افْتَحِ الْكِتَابَ [Open the book], أَغْلِقِ الْكِتَابَ [Close the book], اكْتُبْ [Write], اقْرَأْ [Read], اسْمَعْ [Listen]. Act each command as you say it.

Step 3, Change commands for a girl and for a group. For a girl: اجْلِسِي، قِفِي، اكْتُبِي [Sit, stand, write]. For the whole class: اجْلِسُوا، اكْتُبُوا [Sit, write]. The ending ـِي is for a girl and ـُوا for a group.

Step 4, Role-play a short dialogue. Student: أَيْنَ قَلَمِي؟ [Where is my pen?] Teacher: قَلَمُكَ عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ. [Your pen is on the table.] Student: شُكْرًا. [Thank you.] Teacher: عَفْوًا. [You're welcome.] Swap roles and use a ruler or bag.
Step 5, Fix an error. A teacher tells a girl اجْلِسْ. Correction: to a girl say اجْلِسِي. Another error is saying هَذَا مِسْطَرَةٌ; مِسْطَرَةٌ is feminine, so say هَذِهِ مِسْطَرَةٌ [This is a ruler].

Step 6, Your turn: give three commands to a girl: stand, open the book, write. Model answer: قِفِي. افْتَحِي الْكِتَابَ. اكْتُبِي. [Stand. Open the book. Write.] Then ask where your bag is: أَيْنَ حَقِيبَتِي؟ [Where is my bag?]

modules.title: Food and fruits
modules.outcome: name common foods and say what I like
modules.intro: In this unit, 'Food and fruits', you learn to name common foods and say what I like. Lessons are short and playful, with objects, pictures and talk. You see it, say it, then do it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Food and fruits' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: name common foods and say what I like, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: tuffaha (apple), mawz (banana), burtuqal (orange). Ask: 'Hal tuhibbu al-mawz?' (Do you like bananas?) Method: Model run for 'Food and fruits'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Name common foods and say what I like: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Learn fruit and food words. تُفَّاحٌ [apples], مَوْزٌ [bananas], بُرْتُقَالٌ [oranges], عِنَبٌ [grapes], خُبْزٌ [bread], حَلِيبٌ [milk], مَاءٌ [water], أَرُزٌّ [rice]. Show picture cards and say each word with the right shape in your mouth.

Step 2, Say what you like. أُحِبُّ التُّفَّاحَ. [I like apples.] أُحِبُّ الْمَوْزَ. [I like bananas.] لَا أُحِبُّ الْحَلِيبَ. [I do not like milk.] The thing liked ends with a fatha sound: التُّفَّاحَ، الْمَوْزَ، الْحَلِيبَ.

Step 3, Ask a friend. هَلْ تُحِبُّ الْعِنَبَ؟ [Do you like grapes?] نَعَمْ، أُحِبُّهُ. [Yes, I like it.] لَا، لَا أُحِبُّهُ. [No, I do not like it.] Ask three classmates and record their answers on a tally sheet.

Step 4, Ask for food politely. Child: أُرِيدُ خُبْزًا مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. [I want some bread, please.] Seller: تَفَضَّلْ. [Here you are.] Child: شُكْرًا. [Thank you.] Seller: عَفْوًا. [You're welcome.] Replace خُبْزًا with مَاءً [water] or حَلِيبًا [milk].

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says أُحِبُّ التُّفَّاحُ with a damma ending. Correction: after أُحِبُّ the thing liked takes fatha, so say أُحِبُّ التُّفَّاحَ. Remember to speak to a girl with مِنْ فَضْلِكِ.

Step 6, Your turn: say you like oranges and do not like rice, then ask for water. Model answer: أُحِبُّ الْبُرْتُقَالَ. لَا أُحِبُّ الْأَرُزَّ. أُرِيدُ مَاءً مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. [I like oranges. I do not like rice. I want water, please.]

modules.title: Songs and short stories
modules.outcome: retell short stories and sing short songs
modules.intro: In this unit, 'Songs and short stories', you learn to retell short stories and sing short songs. Lessons are short and playful, with objects, pictures and talk. You see it, say it, then do it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Songs and short stories' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: retell short stories and sing short songs, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: الولد يلعب في الحديقة. أين يلعب الولد؟ في الحديقة. (The boy plays in the garden. Where does the boy play? In the garden.) Method: Model run for 'Songs and short stories'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Retell short stories and sing short songs: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Listen to a tiny story I made. كَانَتْ قِطَّةٌ صَغِيرَةٌ تَلْعَبُ بِكُرَةٍ. [A small cat was playing with a ball.] تَدَحْرَجَتِ الْكُرَةُ تَحْتَ الْبَابِ. [The ball rolled under the door.] سَاعَدَتْهَا أُخْتُهَا. [Her sister helped her.] فَرِحَتِ الْقِطَّةُ. [The cat was happy.]

Step 2, Answer the question words about the story. مَنْ؟ [Who?] الْقِطَّةُ. [The cat.] مَاذَا؟ [What?] كُرَةٌ. [A ball.] أَيْنَ؟ [Where?] تَحْتَ الْبَابِ. [Under the door.] مَنْ سَاعَدَهَا؟ [Who helped her?] أُخْتُهَا. [Her sister.]

Step 3, Retell with sequence words. أَوَّلًا، لَعِبَتِ الْقِطَّةُ. [First, the cat played.] ثُمَّ تَدَحْرَجَتِ الْكُرَةُ. [Then the ball rolled.] فِي النِّهَايَةِ، فَرِحَتِ الْقِطَّةُ. [In the end, the cat was happy.] Say the three sentences without looking.

Step 4, Sing a simple counting chant. وَاحِدٌ، اثْنَانِ، قِطَّةٌ تَلْعَبُ الْآنَ. [One, two, a cat is playing now.] Clap on each word and repeat. Add actions: roll your hands like a ball for تَلْعَبُ.

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says كَانَ قِطَّةٌ صَغِيرَةٌ with the masculine verb. Correction: the cat is feminine, so the verb takes the feminine ending: كَانَتْ قِطَّةٌ صَغِيرَةٌ. Say each feminine past verb with the ending ـَتْ.

Step 6, Your turn: retell the story in your own words using أَوَّلًا and فِي النِّهَايَةِ. Model answer: أَوَّلًا، لَعِبَتِ الْقِطَّةُ بِالْكُرَةِ. فِي النِّهَايَةِ، سَاعَدَتْهَا أُخْتُهَا. [First, the cat played with the ball. In the end, her sister helped her.]

ladder: L1: say and read familiar words and short sentences.
L2: read short texts and write connected sentences.
L3: write paragraphs and speak on a topic with notes.
L4: write for different purposes and analyse how texts persuade.
L5: write and argue at length; handle unseen texts.
L6 (degree): academic reading, writing and citation.
L7 (postgraduate): publish, teach or translate with expert accuracy.
